scope: Independent factual and answer-uniqueness review of only the eight source questions in output/question-quality/aip-first-eight-semantic-independent-input.json. This is not a review of all 375 AIP questions or of nine locale translations.

items.reason: The current Bedrock guide says HYBRID combines vector embeddings and raw text and is supported for OpenSearch Serverless only when the vector store has a filterable text field. C supplies both conditions; A omits the required field and B/D remain semantic-only.
items.ambiguityAssessment: No competing correct choice: metadata filters and temperature do not add raw-text retrieval.

items.reason: A selects the EU geographic profile that keeps inference within its geography. D is an independently required data-residency verification: the current support guide explicitly requires GetInferenceProfile from every planned source Region and validation of every destination ARN because availability/destinations can differ by source Region. The API exposes those model ARNs in models[].
items.ambiguityAssessment: A configures geographic routing; D verifies the actual source-specific candidate set. They are complementary controls, not alternative complete solutions. B/C can use Global destinations and E loses the required automatic cross-Region distribution.

items.reason: Current setup guidance lists G1 at 1536 dimensions and V2 at 1024/512/256, and requires a vector field matching the chosen dimensions. A creates/associates the separate 512-dimensional index while preserving the old one; C repopulates it with document and query embeddings in V2's common space.
items.ambiguityAssessment: The two selected options deliberately divide index/knowledge-base setup from re-embedding and query generation. The wording does not require either individual option to be a complete cutover procedure. B/D/E create incompatible or mixed embedding spaces.

items.reason: The deletion guide states RETAIN keeps all data when the data source is deleted and does not delete the vector store. The S3 connector describes the deletion policy as choosing whether vector-store embeddings are deleted or retained. Deleting a knowledge-base data-source connection is not an S3 object deletion operation, so the stated source-object retention is satisfied unless an independent S3 delete/lifecycle action is introduced.
items.ambiguityAssessment: RETAIN is not a guarantee against external S3 lifecycle deletion, but no option or premise introduces one; DELETE alternatives fail the explicit vector-retention requirement.

items.reason: The current lifecycle policy applies to models launched on or after 2026-09-07. In Legacy, new fine-tuning jobs and new Provisioned Throughput are prohibited; EOL requests fail absent a private provider arrangement, and migration is not automatic. D is the supported pre-EOL migration path.
items.ambiguityAssessment: Existing deployments may continue temporarily, but that does not make A/B viable for the stated recurring customization and uninterrupted future service. C cannot restore Active status.

items.reason: AgentCore preserves context across invocations with the same application-provided runtimeSessionId and isolates each session's compute, memory, and filesystem. B scopes one ID to one intake case and reuses it only for related turns, separating concurrent cases by the same user.
items.ambiguityAssessment: The source's backend mapping responsibility does not imply one global session per user. A loses case isolation, C loses context reuse, and D supplies only a runtime identifier rather than a session boundary.

items.reason: For function-details action groups, the documented functionResponse contract contains responseState and responseBody. REPROMPT passes a response string to the model for invalid input; FAILURE raises DependencyFailedException for a dependency failure. A matches the invalid business-date premise exactly.
items.ambiguityAssessment: The choice names the intended response fields rather than claiming a flattened wire format; full nesting is not contradicted. B/C/D either misclassify the condition or use the API-schema contract.

items.reason: The current Flow guide requires exactly one input node; it receives InvokeFlow content, validates the declared type, and forwards it. Each downstream node input uses an expression to extract the relevant portion of the whole input and then validates that result's type. B defines the object entrance; E maps customerId and question to the separate Lambda and Prompt contracts.
items.ambiguityAssessment: B and E are complementary layers, not competing standalone designs. E does not itself define the single Object input or InvokeFlow content contract; C assumes an unsupported automatic object-to-prompt-variable expansion. A violates the one-input-node rule and D ignores request values.

summary.multipleChoiceMethod: For d1-006, d1-014, and d2-016, the two selections are assessed against the actual question as complementary configuration/verification components. No unsupported assumption that each selected statement alone must implement every stage was applied.

timestampBoundary: reviewedAt is agent-reported metadata; rootCollectedAt is the parent-observed collection time. No verification of the reported reviewer wall-clock time is claimed.
